items.title: Phil Flanigan interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: One time he came out, we were playing the big music hall in Philadelphia, Symphony Hall I believe it’s called.

ctx.x: What was it like to play behind Benny Goodman?

Great. What could I tell you. I mean he always played good. You’ve heard all the stories about the ray and all the unthinking, careless things that he would do, the thoughtless things that he would do. And he acted very strange on any number of occasions. One time he came out, we were playing the big music hall in Philadelphia, Symphony Hall I believe it’s called. Beautiful place. He comes out, the whole band is on stage, he walks out, uproarious applause, applause fades down, he’s holding his little clarinet…

[whistles] almost like he’s testing the acoustics or something. And the whole audience, including the band is sitting there scratching their heads going okay. And this goes on for like a minute and a half, two minutes, right at the beginning of the show. And then finally he just said “Hello. Good evening. It’s so nice to be here. Where are we anyway?” But I viewed him as sort of a harmless sort of a talented idiot savant sort of. You know there’s a lot of artists like that. They’re brilliant artists, socially…
